pullRequest.title: Let load take a path
pullRequest.author: contributor-login
pullRequest.description:
Closes #250.

`load` now takes a path as well as a binary file object: a `pathlib.Path` or a `str` names the file to read.

Timed by hand on my machine: loading `benchmark/data.toml` 100 times took 0.41 s by path and 0.41 s from an open file.
pullRequest.head: load-path

issues.title: Accept a path in `load`
issues.body:
`tomli.load` takes only a binary file object, so every caller writes `with open(path, "rb") as f: tomli.load(f)`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `load` accepts a `pathlib.Path` and parses the file it names.
- [ ] `load` accepts a path given as `str` or as `bytes`.
- [ ] Passing a file opened in text mode still raises the `TypeError` that says to open it in binary mode.
- [ ] Type checkers accept a path argument to `load`.
- [ ] Loading by path is no slower than loading from an open file.
- [ ] The README's "Parse a TOML file" section shows loading a path.
